title: Qualify and version the shared agent lifecycle contract
body:
## Outcome
Define one evidence-backed event and session vocabulary for local Codex Desktop, Codex CLI, and Claude Code that every device integration can consume.

## Scope
This owns shared provider qualification previously planned in Pixoo #29. Pixoo retains consumer adoption in [divoom-app-upgrade#29](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/29). Use the existing Nanoleaf behavior and tests as evidence, without treating its Codex-specific assumptions as universal.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Record accessible installed client versions, primary documentation, event/payload/ordering identifiers, delivery support, and parent/subagent evidence. Distinguish documented, observed, unsupported and inaccessible signals; documentation/fixtures do not establish live compatibility.
- [ ] Define a versioned runtime-validated metadata envelope with provider, host/source, session and available turn identity, event identity or deterministic deduplication fallback, event kind, observation time and evidenced parent relationships.
- [ ] Keep activity, continuing questions, blocked input/approval, turn-ended notices, interruption/runtime end, acknowledgment and freshness distinct. A turn ending proves neither success nor readership.
- [ ] Represent each top-level session separately, including concurrent sessions in one project. Aggregate only attributable children; unknown parentage and unavailable counts stay explicit.
- [ ] Define optional Codex Desktop unread evidence and per-consumer notice policies. Preserve Nanoleaf's existing read behavior during migration; Pixoo dismissal remains monitor-only and never edits agent read state.
- [ ] Allow only lifecycle metadata, identifiers, timestamps and explicit user-chosen labels. Exclude prompts, transcripts, tool arguments/results, auto-copied titles, credentials and unrelated private paths before transmission and persistence.
- [ ] Specify bounded nonblocking fail-open producer delivery, timeout/overflow behavior and silent observational output. Monitoring cannot approve, deny, change permissions or hold an agent action waiting.
- [ ] Provide fixtures for new/old turns, ongoing questions, blocked input, resolution, turn end, interruption, children, duplicates, missing IDs, late events and unsupported evidence. Define required-client stop conditions.
- [ ] Publish vocabulary, schema compatibility rules and source/version evidence in hub documentation and issue-linked OpenSpec artifacts. Mark all live-client gaps for [agent-device-hub#8](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/8) and device acceptance.

## Dependencies
- [agent-device-hub#1](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/1)

## Verification
Schema/fixture validation and a primary-source capability matrix using synthetic metadata. Inspect accessible installed client artifacts read-only; no settings changes or agent launches.

## Delivery target
Source-only, including configuration/installation tooling. Personal setup, agent launches and physical tests need separate explicit authorization.

## Planning and delivery
GitHub owns scope, acceptance, dependencies and status. Follow this repository's AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md. The current request authorizes this backlog definition and repository setup; it does not authorize implementing these future features.

Before implementation, prepare the exact issue-linked OpenSpec change at openspec/changes/gh-2-agent-lifecycle-contract/. Verify the identity and applicable design requirements first.

## Codex-first goal alignment, 2026-09-07

Part of [the shared Codex-integration goal](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/32). First deliver automatic Codex task integration and manual frontend controls for that integration. General agent-independent device control is [a later phase](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/31). Existing local MCP delivery and independently owned work keep their scope. Shared provider contracts remain extensible; retain existing Claude criteria and report Codex milestone evidence separately rather than falsely closing outstanding provider acceptance.

### Additional acceptance criteria
- [ ] Qualify Codex Desktop and CLI on the supported Windows/WSL paths first, including installed-version gaps. Define shared labels, task/project identity and notice acknowledgment needed by manual integration controls without exporting private Codex metadata.
- [ ] Supply the event semantics and supported path matrix needed to establish cold/warm hook baselines in [performance qualification](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/30); document hard fail-open behavior before runtime implementation.

This update defines backlog work only. It does not start implementation, change an active installation or grant device-test authority. Existing OpenSpec identities, validation and UI/physical acceptance gates remain.

title: Implement the reusable agent-state core and provider emitters
body:
## Outcome
Interpret agent observations once and expose durable, trustworthy session snapshots to multiple device consumers.

## Scope
Implement shared TypeScript packages and bounded provider emitters from [agent-device-hub#2](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/2). The first production host is Pixoo's existing backend in [divoom-app-upgrade#31](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/31); this issue does not create a second backend or install hooks.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Implement the qualified provider mappings and deterministic reducer with injectable time. Namespace state by provider/source/session and retain available turn and evidenced child identity.
- [x] Preserve continuing questions, blocked attention, turn-ended notices, interruption and unavailable evidence independently. A new turn or explicit monitor acknowledgment clears only the intended monitor notice.
- [x] Reject stale prior-turn changes, deduplicate retries and make child counts stable under concurrent, missing-ID and reordered observations. Unknown ordering remains visible as uncertainty.
- [x] Expose session observation age separately from collector health. Five minutes without session evidence marks observations uncertain, not failed. Restart restores previously active sessions as uncertain until fresh evidence.
- [x] Persist state, chosen labels and undismissed notices through the host's storage boundary. Bound the diagnostic journal to 24 hours or 10,000 events, whichever comes first, without deleting current state or notices.
- [x] Validate/strip non-allowlisted fields before delivery and persistence. Privacy-canary tests must prove excluded payloads do not appear in transport, storage, diagnostics or errors.
- [x] Export an embedding API for ingest, snapshots/change subscriptions, acknowledgment, shutdown, and migrations. Version the package/contracts and test the TypeScript and Python consumer fixtures; no per-device copy of the reducer.
- [x] Keep provider emitters fail-open with bounded latency, payloads and queues during collector outages. State collection never commands a device, including in Media/Free modes.
- [x] Document immutable snapshot revisions, compatibility, storage ownership, source installation identity and one active state owner. Publish reproducible package artifacts usable by a separate repository without checkout-relative imports.

## Dependencies
- [agent-device-hub#2](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/2)

## Verification
Fake-clock reducer, privacy, deduplication, retention, migration, interrupted-write, restart, concurrent-producer and package-consumer checks without credentials or devices.

title: Define versioned controller capabilities and integration APIs
body:
## Outcome
Give shared clients a stable way to inspect and command existing device owners without erasing device-specific behavior.

## Scope
Own schemas and cross-language fixtures for device identity, capabilities, observations, commands and feeds. Device implementations remain in [divoom-app-upgrade#37](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/37) and [codex-nanoleaf#28](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/28). This contract can be defined independently of provider qualification.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Define a stable configured device ID and controller/source identity. Register only explicitly configured destinations; callers cannot choose raw IPs, URLs, filesystem paths, firmware/reset operations or arbitrary device commands.
- [ ] Describe supported capabilities and typed operations for power/brightness and optional device-specific media, zones, scenes and previews. Unsupported capabilities are explicit; ordinary lights do not implement Pixoo's RGB animation interface.
- [ ] Separate desired configuration, queued/pending work, last successful send, failed/partially applied or uncertain work, external control, and observation age from service health. Transport acknowledgment is never optical proof.
- [ ] Version request/result and snapshot/change-feed envelopes. Include request identity, configuration revision, output generation, typed failure and possible prior effects; define bounded replay, conflicting duplicates, cursor expiry and full resync.
- [ ] Define a machine-client authentication boundary distinct from browser Origin/editing tokens, loopback defaults, credential rotation/revocation and bounded admission. Do not weaken existing browser protections.
- [ ] Keep one designated writer per physical device. Clients delegate through its services/queue; expired generations and reconnects cannot replay stale commands or reclaim ownership.
- [ ] Specify renderer metadata with explicit clock domain, epochs, compatibility and update outcomes. Device payloads may contain Pixoo frames or Nanoleaf zone timelines; no universal animation scheduler is introduced.
- [ ] Define package/API compatibility policy and shared fixtures consumed by Python and TypeScript. Keep databases private to their owners; Windows and WSL must never coordinate by concurrently opening a mounted SQLite file.

## Dependencies
- [agent-device-hub#1](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/1)

## Verification
Schema and contract-consumer fixtures covering unsupported capabilities, replay/conflicts, stale generations/cursors, authentication, unknown telemetry and cross-process clock interpretation.

## Delivery target
Source-only, including configuration/installation tooling. Personal setup, agent launches and physical tests need separate explicit authorization.

## Planning and delivery
GitHub owns scope, acceptance, dependencies and status. Follow this repository's AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md. The current request authorizes this backlog definition and repository setup; it does not authorize implementing these future features.

Before implementation, prepare the exact issue-linked OpenSpec change at openspec/changes/gh-4-controller-contract/. Verify the identity and applicable design requirements first.

## Priority and access decision
Local Codex control is the current delivery priority. Phone, mobile browser, ChatGPT web, and another-computer access are future goals. Keep native-client authentication, explicit targets, and one existing device writer. Local client access may use the existing same-machine Windows/WSL route and does not prohibit the owning controller from reaching its configured LAN device. This contract is the shared source prerequisite for the local MCP module in #7 and [Nanoleaf controller #28](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/28). Provider qualification and standalone hosting are independent.

title: Host shared monitoring and route commands to existing controllers
body:
## Outcome
Provide one optional standalone hub host for shared agent state, registered controllers, APIs and future clients.

## Scope
Compose the shared state core and controller clients. Before this migration the state core can remain embedded in Pixoo. Standalone hosting is an explicit source/deployment stage, not a second simultaneously active collector.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Serve authenticated loopback APIs and revisioned snapshot/change feeds using the shared contracts. Keep agent-state health and each device's health independent.
- [ ] Connect the Pixoo and Linux/WSL Nanoleaf controller APIs through bounded clients; support simulators and deterministic outages without credentials.
- [ ] Route all commands to their existing owner. Isolate queues/failures per device so an offline Pixoo cannot block Nanoleaf; no direct protocol writer is added.
- [ ] Implement one authoritative agent-state owner, whether embedded or standalone. Specify a quiesced, versioned export/import that preserves identities and revisions, switches producers and consumer endpoints, and supports rollback without two active owners or duplicate notices/effects. Exercise Pixoo #31's embedded/remote session-source facade: its renderer/browser must receive the new feed, and shared label/acknowledgment writes must reach the selected owner. Resume ingestion only after the selected owner and consumer routes are ready; fail explicitly if readiness or migration fails.
- [ ] Preserve private data ownership across host changes; do not mount a shared SQLite database between Windows and WSL. Resolve reachability through explicit supported local endpoints without router/firewall changes or an implicit host switch.
- [ ] On restart/reconnect, recover current snapshots and uncertain observations without replaying expired animations, missed pictures or ambiguous sent commands.
- [ ] Package a reproducible host with isolated runtime storage, readiness, graceful shutdown and a controller compatibility matrix. Source completion does not install or start it on the user's machine.

- [ ] Route Pixoo monitor filters/modes and Nanoleaf supported integration settings through their owning APIs. Specify finite versioned integration extensions and compatibility fixtures; do not silently broaden released device API v1, pass native credentials to the browser or add a second device writer.

- [ ] Expose only supported explicit controls and validated links to existing device editors. Preserve Nanoleaf Work/Quiet/Free and Pixoo Monitor/Media meanings; do not introduce a global mode that silently takes over devices.

## Outcome

## Scope

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Establish repeatable Linux baselines in Ubuntu WSL under comparable host/load conditions; no native Windows comparison or executable-forwarding measurement is required. Record client/runtime/repository versions, host/load profile, cold and warm startup, sample counts and repeated runs. Separate hook return, event admission/reduction/publication, each consumer's admission, transport submission and later physical observation.
- [ ] Freeze numeric p95/p99 budgets and hard failure timeouts before implementation based on measured baselines and the user's no-performance-regression requirement. Specify clock comparison, sampling, pass/fail tolerance, CPU/memory/queue limits and intentional rendering cadence. Material budget changes require documented review, not post-failure relaxation.
- [ ] Exercise one task, 10 concurrent tasks and a 50-task burst with Pixoo/Nanoleaf consumers and a stalled third fake consumer. Respect device display capacity and verify bounded overflow/coalescing/resync behavior; these profiles do not promise 50 visible task slots.
- [ ] Prove a stalled or disconnected device cannot delay a healthy consumer or agent hook return. Hooks meet their bounded fail-open budget during host failure; sustained overload keeps memory/queue depth bounded and reports data loss or resync honestly.
- [ ] Measure the real Linux hook from process launch through return, including stdin parsing, admission/commit and actual Linux worker-spawn handoff. Measure Node/Python component and process overhead on Linux; report background readiness/cleanup separately. Use synthetic stdin and explicit disposable Linux state, prove confinement against private state, external network, devices and Windows executables, and reap detached descendants on success, timeout and failure. Admission-only/no-op-launch timing is insufficient. Qualify the monitoring feed independently from manual MCP transport; avoid per-event process creation if it exceeds the budget.
- [ ] Include the shared frontend open/closed and reconnecting, concurrent integration controls, Pixoo playback and Nanoleaf animation/scene regressions, embedded hosting, standalone hosting, restart and rollback.
- [ ] Publish reproducible commands and a pinned cross-repository receipt, distinguish fixture/transport/optical measurements and feed results into #9 and device acceptance. ## Accepted direction
- Keep Node.js/TypeScript shared services and Pixoo, and the Python Windows Nanoleaf worker. Preserve performance through measured release budgets.

- Each device integration consumes the shared feed and retains its own rendering policy, private state and designated writer. One stalled device must not delay another or block Codex.
- Preserve existing local MCP delivery and other coordinators' work. This planning goal does not take over their issues or installed state.

## First-phase frontend
Show Codex sessions, attention, retained notices, freshness, collector/consumer health and device integration state. Support explicit user labels, monitor-only notice dismissal, supported per-device participation/modes and task/project mappings. Device modes keep their existing meanings. Existing advanced editors remain usable; full wall-map/playlist-editor migration, custom effects and exact optical previews are not initial gates.

## Delivery stages
1. Qualify Codex Desktop/CLI and Windows/WSL paths in #2; retain provider-neutral contracts and existing Claude source fixtures without making a new Claude installed rollout the Codex milestone.
2. Deliver #3 and Pixoo #29/#31/#37, then Pixoo #32/#33 and Nanoleaf #29/#49 after their prerequisites.

4. Deliver #6's Codex-integration frontend using the owning controller APIs; deliver #13's shared MCP composition without duplicating existing local tools.

- [ ] Frontend integration controls use protected owning services, preserve identity/revisions and show pending/conflict/uncertain results. Inspection is free of device mutations.
- [ ] Performance budgets pass across required source/runtime profiles; a third fake consumer demonstrates extensibility without adding new production hardware.
- [ ] Source completion is reported separately from installed acceptance. Full Codex-first acceptance needs the approved real Windows/WSL client and device evidence. Claude-specific outstanding criteria remain tracked and are not falsely closed by the Codex milestone.

## Dependencies and delivery target

## Delivery and authority

## Outcome and scope

Reduce GitHub Actions minutes for agent-device-hub while retaining every existing test, package-consumer check, and supported OS/Python combination on PRs and main. The accepted approach removes duplicate runs and compilation before considering any coverage reduction.

Planning baseline, refreshed September 10, 2026: main `396c36aed74cf1d016564536eca13bb16f89834b` still triggers Checks on every push and pull request. [Successful core run 34426914343](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/actions/runs/34426914343) used approximately 13 raw runner-minutes, or 18 minutes after rounding each job upward. This is CI/tooling work with no product behavior or wire-contract delta; record that reason rather than inventing product OpenSpec scenarios.

## Planned implementation

Deliver two sequential PRs linked to this issue, keeping it open until both are verified.

1. Restrict push validation to `main`, preserve existing PR events, add workflow-level cancellation of superseded PR runs, and set ten-minute core job timeouts. Preserve matrix entries, job names, action pins, permissions, commands, and `fail-fast: false`. Apply equivalent scheduling to the guide workflow in coordination with PR #82. Use concurrency group `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}` with `cancel-in-progress: true`; main runs remain independent, and matrix siblings must not cancel one another.
2. Build once per product job, retain its typecheck, and call build-free test variants. Add `:built` variants for `test:contracts`, `test:package`, `test:mcp`, `test:mcp:protocol`, `test:mcp:package`, `test:lifecycle`, and `test:lifecycle:package`. Each original command continues to build before invoking its variant, preserving clean-checkout developer behavior. Retain isolated archive installation, manifest/hash verification, full consumer tests, and consumer typechecking. Add setup-python pip download caching with `requirements-contracts.txt` as the dependency key; keep dependency installation, `npm ci`, and existing npm caching.

Do not remove tests, introduce path-based skipping, reduce platform/version coverage, defer coverage to scheduled runs, share compiled output or installed dependencies between jobs, change runner/billing/privacy settings, weaken merge gates, install software on personal devices, or operate devices. Browser caching, job consolidation, and artifact-retention changes are outside this item.

## Acceptance criteria and verification

- [x] An ordinary update to an open PR runs each applicable workflow once through `pull_request`, with no duplicate branch-push run. A merge to main still runs every configured validation job. Verify workflow configuration and hosted run event/head associations during normal delivery.
- [x] A superseded PR workflow can be cancelled without cancelling another PR, a main run, another workflow, or matrix siblings. Add focused configuration regression coverage and inspect natural overlapping hosted PR updates. If no overlap occurs, explicitly record runtime cancellation as unobserved; static checks alone do not prove scheduler behavior.
- [x] Every core job has a ten-minute timeout; the guide job retains its existing ten-minute timeout. Verify configuration without deliberately running a hung hosted job.
- [x] All 12 core job identities and the Ubuntu/Windows, Python 3.12/3.14, Node 24 coverage remain. Retain the guide job when introduced. Require successful current-head and merged-revision hosted jobs under existing delivery policy.
- [x] The core workflow performs 10 full builds rather than 32, with one build before each product job's tests and one typecheck per product job. Verify script expansion and build-before-test ordering. Compare test inventories/results between original standalone commands and the optimized sequence; a failed build must prevent downstream tests from running against stale output.
- [x] Existing standalone test commands work from a clean build state. All archive-consumer, tamper/hash, TypeScript, Python, and MCP protocol checks retain their behavior. Build-free variants consume only output freshly produced in the same job; do not reuse another run's output.
- [x] Python cache misses still install dependencies and pass tests; cache keys distinguish supported runtimes/platforms and dependency changes. No credentials, private state, or compiled artifacts enter new caches. Inspect setup-python cache configuration and normal hosted cold/warm evidence where available.
- [x] Report before/after job and step durations, raw runner-minutes, and rounded minutes by OS from comparable successful runs. Exclude billing-blocked runs from performance comparisons. Removing duplicate events should halve validation copies for an open-PR update; a one-update PR plus merge drops from three copies to two. These are scheduling estimates, not a guaranteed invoice reduction. Report additional build savings as measured, without a speculative target.
- [x] Update development documentation for equivalent CI commands and complete the work-guide maintenance record and affected inputs/output under delivery authority. Preserve guide browser checks and review-artifact retention.

Planned checks, not executed as part of issue publication: Node 24 `npm ci`, `npm run check:workflow`, `npm run test:workflow`, `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, all existing controller-contract, lifecycle, MCP and isolated-package commands, plus focused CI regression checks. Use Python 3.12 and 3.14 in the hosted matrix. Follow the work-guide procedure for generator, maintenance and browser verification where applicable, and report the actual specification inventory.

No incoming implementation prerequisite was identified. [PR #82](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/82) owns the proposed guide workflow; coordinate its scheduling changes without taking over its branch or requiring unrelated guide/UI delivery first. The core optimization can proceed independently. Reconcile the guide workflow before claiming this issue's full scheduling scope complete. The second PR follows the first as the selected measurement and review sequence, not as a separate cross-issue dependency.

Use one coordinating writer for root scripts, manifests and CI. Refresh main, open PRs and affected instructions before editing. Preserve concurrent ownership and use isolated worktrees.

- Uncertainty: low. Coverage preferences are settled and repeated triggers/builds are visible in source and hosted evidence. Remaining bounded questions are actual savings, cache effectiveness, and observable cancellation; resolve through configuration checks and normal hosted delivery evidence.

Independent Standards and Specification reviewers must inspect the same committed base/head. Include concurrency and package-consumer compatibility in review scope. No new UI behavior is planned; any scope expansion into UI retains the repository's human approval gate. Close only after both PRs and their merged-revision CI satisfy acceptance. Recover regressions through a reviewed revert of the affected workflow/script change, preserving tests and coordinating shared files; do not bypass CI to recover.

title: Re-evaluate Linux performance budgets and reduce hub memory use
body:
## Outcome
Re-evaluate the Linux/WSL performance budgets and reduce standalone hub memory use with reproducible measurements.

## Context and owner decision
During [Hub #5](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/5), the synthetic host workload completed 9,000 ingest/read pairs but reached 164.82 MiB peak RSS against the original 128 MiB service constraint. Four further diagnostic variants also exceeded that constraint. The receipts are retained in [PR #121](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/121), under `apps/hub/evidence/`.

The owner explicitly requested doubling the service RSS limit to **256 MiB** and creating this backlog item. This is a deliberate budget revision, not evidence that memory use improved. Preserve the original receipts and their failed results against 128 MiB. This follow-up is not a prerequisite for #5; that issue still requires its remaining functional acceptance and validation against the revised budget. Hook latency/CPU/child-RSS limits, queue/body limits and deadlines are unchanged by this decision.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Audit the scope and rationale of the existing budgets: service RSS versus JavaScript heap and native allocations, full-hook latency/CPU versus API timings, startup versus steady state, and isolated versus combined service memory.
- [ ] Define representative Linux/WSL workloads, including 1/10/50 sessions, longer-running steady state, bounded journal growth, SSE clients, replay retention and controller outages. Record versions, load, sampling and measurement boundaries.
- [ ] Profile allocations and retention to identify the causes of the observed memory use. Distinguish startup/JIT overhead, transient allocation, native SQLite/network allocations and leaks using evidence.
- [ ] Implement measured memory improvements without weakening durability, ownership, privacy, fail-open deadlines, retention or failure isolation. Retain before/after receipts and every failed trial.
- [ ] Propose justified service and end-to-end budgets with explicit headroom and regression checks. Retain 256 MiB until a separately reviewed change replaces it; do not silently rewrite historical results.
- [ ] Align the budget artifact, documentation and qualification checks with [integrated performance #30](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/30). Distinguish partial API measurements from full integrated qualification.

## Scope and verification
Linux in WSL is primary. Native Windows qualification, installation, live state migration and physical-device testing are outside this source follow-up. Use disposable state and fake controllers. Require independent review and applicable CI for future implementation.

Related: [Pixoo performance hardening #61](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/61). Coordinate shared measurement boundaries without absorbing that separately owned work.

## Planning
Backlog only; this issue does not start its implementation. Before implementation, prepare an issue-linked OpenSpec change if required by `docs/sdlc.md`.
